item: A re-index writes only the mention rows that changed, and the drain reports what it kept, updated, removed and added
summary: Lenovo's drain ran at 7,673 articles an hour (2.1 a second) because every re-indexed article deleted and re-inserted about 80 mention rows through ten indexes in a 41 GB encrypted file. index_article now reads the article's rows once and writes the difference: an unchanged row keeps its id and created_at, a changed row is updated in place under its id and stamped now, a gone row is deleted, a new one inserted; every stored column but identity and write time is compared. The drain's stats gain rows kept, updated, removed and added and a split of the apply time. A resumed drain that walked a batch always ends with its corpus-epoch bump. On a sandbox pass where every row was unchanged the mention SQL fell from 9.5 s to 1.1 s.
